title: What Does an Observability Foundation Model Know?
claim: Linear readouts from a pretrained model's hidden states beat the strongest raw-input baselines for some labels, but not all.
layout: 4 panels in a row, shared rows, dashed reference line at the main model's mean
description: Four side-by-side dot plots, one for each taxonomy label: Cadence, Metric type, Domain and Cardinality. Each panel shares the same six rows: Toto, Best raw window, Block perm., Random init., Six-stat. probe and Shuffled. The x-axis is held-out test macro-F1, running from about 0.2 to 1.0. Toto is a bold dark-blue circle, and a dashed vertical line extends from it through each panel. The strongest raw-window baseline is an orange square labelled with the model's name (FNO or GBDT). The other baselines are small gray dots with error bars. Toto sits to the right of the orange square for Cadence and Metric type. The two are roughly tied for Domain. For Cardinality the orange FNO square is far to the right of Toto. The eye goes first to the blue dot and the dashed line, then to the orange squares.
caption: Held-out test macro-F1 of Toto, its baselines, and the shuffled-label floor for each taxonomy label (means ± half-widths over five resplits; §4). The dashed line marks Toto’s mean; the orange square is the strongest raw-window model for that label.
abstract: A linear probe can show that a label is recoverable from a model's hidden states, but not whether that goes beyond what the input already reveals, or whether the model uses it. We audit Toto, an observability forecasting foundation model, on the Benchmark of Observability Metrics (BOOM) across five series-disjoint resplits, comparing linear probes on its frozen residual stream with models that read the raw input window and with Toto's architecture stripped of its trained configuration. Short-vs-medium cadence and metric type are more linearly recoverable from Toto's residuals than from the strongest raw-window model in every resplit (macro-F1 0.766 vs. 0.633 and 0.545 vs. 0.498). Domain is nearly tied, and series cardinality is recovered far better from the raw window. MOMENT-base shows related cadence, metric-type, and domain readouts. Recoverability is not use: exchanging Toto's residuals with those of high-burst donors moves a future-burstiness readout as intended but does not make forecasts consistently burstier than a randomized donor. A BOOM-trained coordination probe has negative zero-shot R^2 on the tested external benchmarks. We report each label against its strongest baseline.
